PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-08-12
48M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling generally well with good energy at work and home. Denies chest pain. No shortness of breath. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and takeout, which was discussed. He works as a long-haul driver with long periods of sitting and irregular meals. Sleep is about 6 hours most nights. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol. No new concerns today.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 198 lb, BMI 29.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): Hgb 12.6 g/dL, A1c 6.1%, lipid panel within goal, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks, packing meals for the road, and adding short walks during breaks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
2. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron every other day to reduce stomach upset. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
3. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed; FIT kit provided. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Encouraged regular physical activity and adequate hydration on the road.
4. Lifestyle: reviewed strategies for healthier choices during long shifts and the importance of regular breaks, adequate sleep, and staying hydrated while driving. Encouraged stretching at rest stops.

Return in 6 months to review A1c, sooner as needed.
